title: Estate and Successor Services Handbook: An Extension Request Carried Over to the Estate in Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases
content:
**The request and the date of death.** For the first extension on a Cedarline Summit loan's Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases case whose borrower has died:

- The extension request considered is the most recently received request on the case still awaiting a decision. Among requests received on the same day, it is the one recorded later by its recorded date and time.
- The date of death is read from the accepted death notice on the borrower's occupancy profile (Occupancy and Residency Certification). Where more than one accepted death notice is on the profile, the date of death is read from the one received most recently. Among accepted notices received on the same day, it is read from the one recorded later by its recorded date and time.

**Rule.**

- Where the extension request was filed by the borrower of record, and the borrower's date of death on the accepted death notice falls after the day the request was received, 10 calendar days are added to the extension length for carrying the request over to the estate.
- Where the request was filed by someone other than the borrower of record, 5 calendar days are added to it.
- Where the borrower of record filed it and the request was received on or after the date of death, or no date of death is on an accepted death notice, nothing is added.

| Who filed the request | Request received compared with the date of death | Days added |
|---|---|---|
| the borrower of record | before the date of death | 10 |
| the borrower of record | on or after the date of death | 0 |
| the borrower of record | no date of death on an accepted notice | 0 |
| anyone else | any | 5 |

## Boundary (hypothetical)

A borrower files a request received on 11 August and dies on 12 August. The death falls after the receipt day, so 10 days are added. Had the death been on 11 August, nothing would be added.
